items.front: How do you combine a:b and b:c into a:b:c?
items.back: Scale each so the shared term b matches (use the LCM of the b-terms), then read a:b:c. For 2:3 and 4:5 this gives 8:12:15.
items.source: APPSC Quantitative Reasoning — Types of Ratios

items.front: Compound ratio of a:b, c:d, e:f?
items.back: (a × c × e) : (b × d × f) — the product of the first terms to the product of the second terms, then simplify.
items.source: APPSC Quantitative Reasoning — Types of Ratios

items.back: Third to a, b = b × b ÷ a; fourth to a, b, c = b × c ÷ a; mean proportional of a, b = √(a × b). In any proportion a × d = b × c.
Direct: x ÷ y stays constant (more gives more). Inverse: x × y stays constant (more gives less), as with men × days.

items.front: Componendo & dividendo, and its typical use?
items.back: If a/b = c/d then (a + b)/(a − b) = (c + d)/(c − d). It turns a sum-to-difference ratio into the base ratio: (m + n):(m − n) = 7:3 gives m:n = 5:2.
items.source: APPSC Quantitative Reasoning — Componendo and Dividendo

items.back: In the ratio of capital × time for each partner; each share = (their term ÷ total) × profit. Equal periods make it the ratio of capitals only.
items.examPoint: Partnership — profit sharing by capital × time

items.back: (size1 × mean1 + size2 × mean2) ÷ (size1 + size2). Never simply average the two means when the group sizes differ.

items.front: Average of equally-spaced numbers; first n natural numbers?
items.back: Equally-spaced average = middle term = (first + last) ÷ 2. Average of the first n natural numbers = (n + 1) ÷ 2.
items.examPoint: Average of first n natural numbers

items.front: Average change on inclusion or replacement of a member?
items.back: New entry = new average × (n + 1) − old average × n. On a swap, new value = old value + (change in average × count), as in the 16th-innings type.
items.examPoint: Average change on inclusion / exclusion / replacement of a member

items.back: quantity(cheaper) : quantity(dearer) = (dearer − mean) : (mean − cheaper). The mean always lies between the two component values.

items.front: Successive replacement of liquid — how much milk is left after n draws?
items.back: milk left = initial × (1 − r/T)^{n}, where r is drawn each time and T is the total. For 20 litres, drawing 4 twice, 20 × (0.8)^{2} = 12.8 litres.
items.examPoint: Successive replacement of liquid in a mixture — (1 − r/T) each step
items.source: APPSC Quantitative Reasoning — Replacement N Times

items.front: Ratio a:b as a percentage of the whole; overlapping-group count?
items.back: a as a percentage of the whole = a ÷ (a + b) × 100, not a ÷ b. Overlap count = (group 1 total + group 2 total) − overall total.
